item.title: Bobo urges Ra to stick to the basics during Farebrother Trophy clash
item.description: The Ra rugby team heads into this week’s Inkk Farebrother Trophy Challenge with grassroots players from the province who have been training together for about three months. Head coach and former Flying Fijians and Fiji 7s player Sireli Bobo says getting the basics right will be crucial this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Ra rugby team heads into this week’s Inkk Farebrother Trophy Challenge with grassroots players from the province who have been training together for about three months.

Head coach and former Flying Fijians and Fiji 7s player Sireli Bobo says getting the basics right will be crucial this week.

Bobo says his players stuck to the basics during their match against Naitasiri, which proved to be the difference when the final whistle blew.

He acknowledges that defending the trophy against a strong Nadroga side will not be easy.

However, he says his players need to build on their previous performance, maintain consistency, trust in the Lord and remain focused on the challenge ahead.

Bobo also thanked the supporters and the Vanua for their continued support, saying the team is looking forward to its next challenge against Skipper Cup champions Nadroga.

Ra will host Nadroga in the second Farebrother Trophy Challenge at Narauyaba in Rakiraki at 3pm.

item.content:encoded:
Crest Fiji A netball player Kiana Toganivalu is eager to sharpen her skills and gain valuable experience when the team competes in the PacificAus Sports Netball Challenge Series in Brisbane, Australia, later this month.

The first-year University of the South Pacific student from Tailevu says one of her main goals is to improve her movement inside the shooting circle instead of relying solely on holding her position.

Tonganivalu says competing at this level will provide valuable exposure and help her develop as a player both on and off the court.

She says her family is proud of her selection, but she understands that continued hard work, discipline and sacrifice will be essential as she prepares for the tournament.

Tonganivalu also acknowledges the unwavering support of her family, coaches and everyone who has played a part in her netball journey since primary school.

The Crest Fiji A team will compete in the PacificAus Sports Netball Challenge Series from 23rd to 28th November at Nissan Arena in Brisbane, Australia.
